leftEvidence.title: Uriah refuses the comforts David arranges

points.label: Action and response
points.left: David summons Uriah, asks about the war, repeatedly sends him home, offers a gift, makes him drunk, and hears Uriah name ark, Israel, Judah, and soldiers in tents.
points.right: David writes Uriah’s death order and sends it by Uriah, Joab positions him, soldiers die, a report is managed, Bathsheba mourns, David takes her into his house, and the LORD is displeased.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places Uriah’s stated solidarity frustrates David’s concealment inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places concealment ends with a narrator’s explicit Godward judgment inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Samuel 11:6–13 and 2 Samuel 11:14–27 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Taking, Rebuke, and House Fracture” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: A sealed order turns battle into arranged death

payload.tension: 2 Samuel 11:6–13 foregrounds Uriah’s stated solidarity frustrates David’s concealment; 2 Samuel 11:14–27 foregrounds concealment ends with a narrator’s explicit Godward judgment. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
